unmapped_findings: Yield ratio (YS/UTS) for the 750 °C, 60 min sample = 0.67 (Table 4), lower than that of the 98% CR sample.
For the sample annealed for 60 min, the contribution from (i) ordering and (ii) solid solution strengthening are the major contributing mechanisms to the yield strength (b0098).
Micro-strain of the 750 °C, 60 min sample = 1.46 × 10^-4 (XRD), a one-order-of-magnitude drop from the 98% CR state (1.46 × 10^-3).

The drastic change in yield strength (1800 MPa for 98% CR to 265 MPa for the 750 °C/60 min anneal) accompanies a dislocation-density change from ~2.2 × 10^15 m^-2 (98% CR) to ~10^12 m^-2 (b0076), identifying dislocation strengthening as a main mechanism.

By Mössbauer spectroscopy the Fe-6.8Al composition shows five hyperfine-field components with B_hf/Area/V_f: 32.68 T (8.55%/7.7%), 30.34 T (45.45%/44%), 27.69 T (23.63%/24.8%), 25.05 T (2.35%/2.6%), 23.26 T (1.26%/1.4%) — the ~23 T component being a possible indicator of a low-volume-fraction Fe3Al phase (Table 1).

Fig. 9 approximate strengthening contributions for the 750 °C/60 min sample (total YS = 265 MPa): lattice frictional stress (small sliver), solid solution ~80 MPa, grain boundary ~200 MPa, thin dislocation band, and an ordering cap completing 265 MPa; error bars associated with grain-boundary and ordered-phase strengthening.

Comparison: Rana et al. [3] reported YS = 342 MPa for Fe-6.8Al annealed at 900 °C for 1 min (ferrite grain size 69.2 ± 34.8 µm), higher than the 265 MPa of this 750 °C/60 min sample, attributed to the higher ferrite grain size in the present case.
The ordered Fe3Al phase size increases with aluminium content; from SAXS it ranges between 2.5 ± 0.15 nm and 3.75 ± 0.2 nm over 5–9 wt% Al (Fig. 4).
